question: Does context and tool availability enable this AI instance to execute known related tasks without follow-up user corrections?

hypotheses.H1: The same underlying model can improve execution with relevant context, prior experience and tools, without weight editing.
hypotheses.H2: Relevant context and tools alone are sufficient for reliable low-intervention completion across typical tasks.

method.design: single model instance plus real GitHub reads and deterministic structural/oracle tests; retrospective failure comparison. No randomized held-out LLM comparison and no live second LLM.
method.query_policy: existing GitHub records as context; no additional external-source web search needed for R01 replay
method.interventions: deliberately corrupted source reference, deliberately stale status, synthetic APP-C outcome states
method.risk: Reusing task data and evaluator construction in same session biases results; policy checks do not demonstrate model reliability.

tool_trace.browser_tool: unavailable outside originating browser context, observed in current turn
tool_trace.independent_model_calls: unavailable (no configured model credentials in local runtime; user was not asked for secrets)
tool_trace.external_research: Separate literature verification of Reflexion, SWE-agent, Mem2ActBench, MemoryAgentBench and invalid memory reuse

conclusion.what_was_tested: context retrieval, status reconciliation, branch conditions, evidence checks, stop boundary
conclusion.what_was_not_tested: user time savings, real LLM A/B, general population, autonomous operation over repeated sessions
conclusion.next_experiment: Run same held-out agent tasks with baseline existing AI vs context-pushed vs tools+pushed vs memory/experience combined, same model and permissions, blind grading; measure interventions and completion accuracy.
